lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-rotation-trace-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For a nondegenerate oriented triangle $K\subset\mathbb R^2$, set $R(a,b)=(-b,a)$, let $n$ be cell-outward and $t=Rn$. If $\sigma\in H(\operatorname{div};K)$ is real, then $R\sigma\in H(\operatorname{curl};K)$, $\operatorname{curl}(R\sigma)=\operatorname{div}\sigma$ distributionally, and $\int_K(R\sigma\cdot R\nabla\phi+\operatorname{curl}(R\sigma)\phi)=\langle\gamma_n\sigma,[\phi]\rangle$ for all $\phi\in H^1(K)$. Thus weak tangential trace equals weak normal trace under $t=Rn$.

Here $H(\operatorname{curl};K):=\{w\in L^2(K;\mathbb R^2):\partial_1w_2-\partial_2w_1\in L^2(K)\}$ with its graph norm. The weak tangential trace is the functional on $H^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ defined by the integral in the Statement; the computation below proves it is the rotation of the PE08 weak normal trace.
def-na-least-squares-poisson-first-order:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be bounded connected Lipschitz and $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Solve $-\Delta u=f$, $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$; set $\sigma=-\nabla u$, so $\operatorname{div}\sigma=f$. For a finite conforming shape-regular triangular mesh, define $X_h=RT_0(\mathcal T_h)\times(P_1(\mathcal T_h)\cap H^1_0(\Omega))$ and $J_h(\sigma_h,u_h)=\|\sigma_h+\nabla u_h\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}\sigma_h-f\|_2^2$. Here $RT_0(K)=P_0(K)^2+xP_0(K)$ and $P_1$ is continuous piecewise affine. The real Sobolev-space and zero-boundary conventions are [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]; H(div), mesh, and RT conventions are [[def-na-hdiv-space]] and [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]]. This is the plan-spec PE30 sign convention; negating the design flux converts its residuals to these and preserves the squared objective. Integrals are exact; geometry, quadrature and roundoff errors are excluded.
def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$, $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral and $\mathcal T_h$ a finite conforming shape-regular simplicial partition; all fields are real. Put $H(div,\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH(div;K)$ and $H^1(\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH^1(K)$, with squared broken graph norm $\sum_K(\|\tau\|_2^2+\|div\tau\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2+\|\nabla v\|_2^2)$. Let $\widehat U$ be the elementwise trace range of $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and $\widehat Q_n$ the elementwise weak normal trace range of $H(div;\Omega)$, each with global lift infimum norm; range membership is compatibility and normal traces are conservative across interior facets. Set $U=L^2(\Omega)^d\times L^2(\Omega)\times\widehat U\times\widehat Q_n$, $V=H(div,\mathcal T_h)\times H^1(\mathcal T_h)$. For $x=(\sigma,u,\widehat u,\widehat\sigma_n)$ and $y=(\tau,v)$, define
$$b(x,y)=(\sigma,\tau)-(u,div_h\tau)+\langle\widehat u,\tau\cdot n\rangle-(\sigma,\nabla_hv)+\langle\widehat\sigma_n,v\rangle,\quad F_f(y)=(f,v).$$
Pairings sum over cell boundaries and use the cell-outward normal. The sign convention is $\sigma=-\nabla u$, $div\sigma=f$.
lem-na-least-squares-poisson-residual-no:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be bounded connected Lipschitz and $C_P$ satisfy $\|w\|_2\le C_P\|
abla w\|_2$ on $H^1_0$. For $z=(\delta\sigma,\delta u)\in H(div)	imes H^1_0$, put $Rz=(\delta\sigma+
abla\delta u,div\delta\sigma)$. This is injective and its norm is equivalent to the product graph norm. If $a=\|R_1z\|_2$, $b=\|R_2z\|_2$, $g=\|
abla\delta u\|_2$, then $g\le a+C_Pb$, $\|\delta u\|_2\le C_P(a+C_Pb)$, $\|\delta\sigma\|_2\le2a+C_Pb$, and $\|Rz\|^2\le2\|z\|^2_{H(div)	imes H^1}$.
alg-na-practical-dpg-finite-riesz-solves:
## Statement

For a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_N$ of a finite real graph-test space $V_r(K)$, form exact Gram entries $G_{ij}=(v_j,v_i)_V$ and $g_i=b_K(w,v_i)$. If $G$ is positive definite, solve $Gc=g$ exactly and return $T_rw=\sum_jc_jv_j$; otherwise return `singular-test-matrix`. No quadrature or rounded solve is included.
lem-na-hdiv-normal-trace-surjectivity:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the scalar trace convention of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open; all spaces are real. With $T_D=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D)$ and its quotient norm, the weak normal trace map
$$\gamma_n:H(\operatorname{div};D)\longrightarrow T_D',\qquad \langle\gamma_n\tau,[w]\rangle=\int_D\bigl(\tau\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}\tau)w\bigr),$$
is onto. In fact every $L\in T_D'$ has a lift $\tau\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$ satisfying $\gamma_n\tau=L$ and $\|\tau\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}\le\|L\|_{T_D'}$.
lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-skeleton-quotie:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. The elementwise trace map $\Gamma_0:H^1_0(\Omega)\to\prod_KH^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ and normal-trace map $\Gamma_n:H(div;\Omega)\to\prod_K(H^1(K)/H^1_0(K))'$ have real Hilbert quotient ranges with global lift infimum norms. These equal the infima over broken extensions whose gluing belongs to the respective global space. Compatibility means membership in these ranges, so normal traces are conservative on interior facets.
rem-na-practical-dpg-roundoff-and-normal:
## Statement

The Fortin, boundedness, and Riesz arguments use exact integrals and exact finite solves; they imply no quadrature or floating-point perturbation estimate. For full-column-rank real $A$, $\kappa_2(A^TA)=\kappa_2(A)^2$.
lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-bilinear-form-b:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. On the real trial and broken graph-test spaces of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]], $b$ is bounded by $|b(x,y)|\le5\|x\|_U\|y\|_V$, uniformly in mesh size.
lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-trial-kernel:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. In the spaces of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]], if $b(x,y)=0$ for every broken test on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, then $x=(\sigma,u,\widehat u,\widehat\sigma_n)=0$.
lem-na-least-squares-poisson-space-confo:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. The finite-mesh family $RT_0(\mathcal T_h)\times(P_1(\mathcal T_h)\cap H^1_0(\Omega))$ from [[def-na-least-squares-poisson-first-order]] is a finite-dimensional subspace of $H(div;\Omega)\times H^1_0(\Omega)$.
lem-na-practical-dpg-fortin-p1-r3:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For trials $P_1(K)^2\times P_1(K)$, continuous trace $\widetilde P_2(\partial K)$ and normal trace $P_1(\partial K)$ on a shape-regular triangular mesh, there is an element-local Fortin map into $P_3(K)^2\times P_3(K)$. It has a mesh-independent broken graph bound, preserves the scalar cell mean, satisfies $\|v-\Pi^{grad}_3v\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(K)}$, and $b(w_h,y-\Pi y)=0$ for all discrete trial tuples and broken tests.
alg-na-ultraweak-poisson-ideal-trial-to-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For the real Hilbert trial/test spaces $U,V$ and bounded form $b$ of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]], define $Tw\in V$ by $(Tw,v)_V=b(w,v)$ for all $v\in V$. Then $T$ is bounded linear and the ideal test space for $U_h$ is $T(U_h)$; this exact definition does not assert practical computability.
thm-na-least-squares-poisson-best-approx:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice required by the weak Poisson supplier. Let $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ on a bounded connected Lipschitz polygon, and let $(\sigma,u)=(-\nabla u,u)$ be the unique weak Dirichlet solution. The exact functional $J_h$ has a unique minimizer in the conforming RT0/P1 family, and that minimizer is the orthogonal best approximation in the residual inner product. Its scalar component remains in $H^1_0(\Omega)$.
lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-bounded-load-li:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the real spaces and signs of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. For every bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedron $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, and every finite conforming shape-regular simplicial mesh, give $U$ the squared product norm from its two $L^2$ factors and two global trace lift-infimum norms, and give $V$ its full broken graph norm. Define $B:U\to V'$ by $(Bx)(y)=b(x,y)$. There is a bounded linear map $R:V'\to U$ such that $BR=I_{V'}$ and $\|R\|\le C_*$. Choose any $C_P>0$ with $\|w\|_2\le C_P\|\nabla w\|_2$ for $w\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, put $a=(C_P^2+2)^{1/2}$, and set $$C_*^2=(1+a)^2+(1+C_Pa)^2+(1+C_P^2)a^2+(\sqrt2+a)^2+1.$$ The constant is independent of the mesh. No simple-connectivity or connected-boundary hypothesis is imposed.
thm-na-ultraweak-poisson-adjoint-graph-i:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For every bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedron $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, and every finite conforming shape-regular simplicial mesh, give $U$ its $L^2$/global-quotient product norm and $V$ the full broken graph norm of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. With $C_*$ from [[lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-bounded-load-lifting]], the primal and adjoint bounds are $$\sup_{y\ne0}\frac{|b(x,y)|}{\|y\|_V}\ge C_*^{-1}\|x\|_U,\qquad \sup_{x\ne0}\frac{|b(x,y)|}{\|x\|_U}\ge C_*^{-1}\|y\|_V.$$ Both constants are independent of the mesh. The bounded operator $B:U\to V'$ and its Riesz trial-to-test map $T:U\to V$ are boundedly invertible, with inverse norms at most $C_*$. No simple-connectivity or connected-boundary hypothesis is required; connected polyhedra with holes are included.
thm-na-ideal-ultraweak-poisson-energy-be:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $x\in U$ be any exact ultraweak solution and let $U_h\subset U$ be finite dimensional. The ideal DPG equations with test space $T(U_h)$ have a unique solution $x_h$, which is the orthogonal projection of $x$ in the induced energy inner product $(w,z)_E=(Tw,Tz)_V$. Consequently $\|x-x_h\|_E=\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_E=\|B(x-x_h)\|_{V'}$.
thm-na-practical-dpg-fortin-quasioptimal:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Assume the form and spaces of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]], a finite conforming triangular mesh, and continuous primal and adjoint graph inf-sup constants with minimum $\beta>0$. Let $U_h\subset U$ consist of volume fields $\sigma_h|_K\in P_1(K)^2$, $u_h|_K\in P_1(K)$, continuous scalar traces $\widehat u_h|_{\partial K}\in\widetilde P_2(\partial K)$, and conservative normal traces $\widehat\sigma_{n,h}|_{\partial K}\in P_1(\partial K)$. This is finite-dimensional. Let $V_r=\prod_K(P_3(K)^2\times P_3(K))$ and let $T_r:U_h\to V_r$ be the finite Riesz map from [[alg-na-practical-dpg-finite-riesz-solves]]. Let $\Pi:V\to V_r$ be the bounded Fortin map of [[lem-na-practical-dpg-fortin-p1-r3]], with $b(U_h,(I-\Pi)V)=0$ and $\|\Pi\|\le C_\Pi$. Then for every bounded load $F\in V'$, the practical DPG system tested with $T_r(U_h)$ has a unique solution $x_h$, and
$$\|x-x_h\|_U\le(1+\|b\|C_\Pi/\beta)\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_U,$$
where $x$ is the exact continuous solution.
thm-na-practical-dpg-residual-estimator-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Assume the continuous trial-to-test operator is boundedly invertible with lower inf-sup constant $\beta>0$, and let $\Pi:V\to V_r$ be the bounded Fortin map with $b(U_h,(I-\Pi)V)=0$. For any exact solution $x=B^{-1}F$ and any $\widetilde x_h\in U_h$, define the practical residual estimator $\eta=\|F-B\widetilde x_h\|_{V_r'}$ and Fortin data oscillation $\operatorname{osc}(F)=\|F\circ(I-\Pi)\|_{V'}$. Then
$$\beta^2\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U^2\le\eta^2+(\|\Pi\|\eta+\operatorname{osc}(F))^2,\quad \eta\le\|b\|\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U,$$
$$\operatorname{osc}(F)\le\|b\|\|I-\Pi\|\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_U.$$
For the stated P1/R3 Poisson Fortin map, $\operatorname{osc}(F_f)\le C(\sum_Kh_K^2\|f-f_K\|_{L^2(K)}^2)^{1/2}$, where $f_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K f$; it vanishes for cellwise constant $f$.
cor-na-practical-dpg-poisson-quasioptima:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be any bounded connected Lipschitz polygon, including polygons with holes, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be any finite conforming shape-regular triangular mesh. Use the exact two-dimensional P1/R3 practical family selected in PE30: volume fields $\sigma_h|_K\in P_1(K)^2$ and $u_h|_K\in P_1(K)$; compatible global scalar traces of degree at most two on facets, zero on boundary facets; conservative global normal traces of degree at most one; and broken tests $V_r=\prod_K(P_3(K)^2\times P_3(K))$, with the graph inner product inherited from $V$. The local Fortin projection $\Pi:V\to V_r$ is that of [[lem-na-practical-dpg-fortin-p1-r3]], and $C_\Pi$ is its operator norm bound. For each $f\in L^2(\Omega)$, the continuous ultraweak solution $x$ and practical solution $x_h$ exist uniquely, with $$\|x-x_h\|_U\le(1+5C_\Pi C_*)\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_U.$$ For every $\widetilde x_h\in U_h$, put $\eta=\|F_f-B\widetilde x_h\|_{V_r'}$, where $V_r'$ is the dual of $V_r$ with its induced norm, and $\operatorname{osc}(F_f)=\|F_f\circ(I-\Pi)\|_{V'}$. Then $$C_*^{-2}\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U^2\le\eta^2+(C_\Pi\eta+\operatorname{osc}(F_f))^2,\qquad \eta\le5\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U,$$ and $$\operatorname{osc}(F_f)\le C_{\rm osc}\left(\sum_Kh_K^2\|f-f_K\|_{L^2(K)}^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad f_K=|K|^{-1}\int_Kf,$$ where $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and $C_{\rm osc}$ is the cellwise constant from the Fortin map's mean-preserving local $L^2$ estimate. The constants $C_*$, $C_\Pi$, and $C_{\rm osc}$ are independent of mesh size for the fixed domain and shape-regular family. The practical corollary is two-dimensional; the continuous graph theorem also covers dimension three.
cex-na-least-squares-boundary-omission-n:
## Statement

If zero boundary values are removed from the continuous first-order Poisson least-squares problem with zero load, every constant scalar $u$ with $\sigma=0$ has zero residual; hence the unconstrained minimizer is not unique.
ex-na-least-squares-poisson-residual-cer:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. On $\Omega=(0,1)^2$ with its two-triangle diagonal mesh, let $u=x(1-x)y(1-y)$, $\sigma=-\nabla u$, and $f=-\Delta u$. Then $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, $\sigma\in H(div;\Omega)$, $\sigma+\nabla u=0$, and $div\sigma-f=0$, so the continuous least-squares residual is zero.
cex-na-practical-dpg-too-small-test-spac:
## Statement

On one triangle, take a four-dimensional trial subspace of $P_1(K)^2\times P_0(K)$ and the three-dimensional constant test space $P_0(K)^2\times P_0(K)$. The practical trial-to-test map has a nontrivial kernel, so the normal equations cannot have a unique trial solution for any load for which a solution exists.
ex-na-ideal-and-practical-dpg-test-vecto:
## Statement

Let $U=V=\mathbb R^2$ with Euclidean inner product, $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $b(x,y)=(Ax)\cdot y$, $U_h=\operatorname{span}(e_2)$, practical test space $V_r=\operatorname{span}(e_1)$, and load $F(y)=e_1\cdot y$. Then $Te_2=(1,1)$, $T^re_2=e_1$, and ideal and practical trial coefficients are $1/2$ and $1$.
